tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-update-data-source
tools.description:
Update a Notion data source's schema, title, attributes, or page layout. Schema changes use SQL DDL statements. Returns Markdown showing updated structure and schema.

Accepts a data source ID (collection ID from fetch response's <data-source> tag) or a single-source database ID. Multi-source databases require the specific data source ID.

The statements param accepts semicolon-separated DDL statements:
- ADD COLUMN "Name" <type> - add a new property
- DROP COLUMN "Name" - remove a property
- RENAME COLUMN "Old" TO "New" - rename a property
- ALTER COLUMN "Name" SET <type> - change type/options. For SELECT/MULTI_SELECT, list every option to keep; omitted options are removed. Existing options keep their id and can be recolored.


The page_layout param replaces the layout every page in the data source uses (pinned properties, sidebar, property sections, and a content tab next to views). Fetch the data source first to get the current layout, then edit it. See notion://docs/database-page-layouts for the format.

Notes: Cannot delete/create title properties. Max one unique_id property. Cannot update synced databases. Use "fetch" first to see current schema and get the data source ID from <data-source url="collection://..."> tags.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-update-data-source
schema.description:
Update a Notion data source's schema, title, attributes, or page layout. Schema changes use SQL DDL statements. Returns Markdown showing updated structure and schema.

Accepts a data source ID (collection ID from fetch response's <data-source> tag) or a single-source database ID. Multi-source databases require the specific data source ID.

The statements param accepts semicolon-separated DDL statements:
- ADD COLUMN "Name" <type> - add a new property
- DROP COLUMN "Name" - remove a property
- RENAME COLUMN "Old" TO "New" - rename a property
- ALTER COLUMN "Name" SET <type> - change type/options. For SELECT/MULTI_SELECT, list every option to keep; omitted options are removed. Existing options keep their id and can be recolored.


The page_layout param replaces the layout every page in the data source uses (pinned properties, sidebar, property sections, and a content tab next to views). Fetch the data source first to get the current layout, then edit it. See notion://docs/database-page-layouts for the format.

Notes: Cannot delete/create title properties. Max one unique_id property. Cannot update synced databases. Use "fetch" first to see current schema and get the data source ID from <data-source url="collection://..."> tags.

data_source_id.description: The data source to update. Accepts a collection:// URI from <data-source> tags, a bare UUID, or a database ID (only if the database has a single data source).

statements.description:
Semicolon-separated SQL DDL statements to update the schema. Supports ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, RENAME COLUMN, and ALTER COLUMN SET.

Property type syntax:
- Simple: TITLE, RICH_TEXT, DATE, PEOPLE, CHECKBOX, URL, EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, STATUS, FILES
- SELECT('opt':color, ...) / MULTI_SELECT('opt':color, ...)
- NUMBER [FORMAT 'dollar'] / FORMULA('expression')
- RELATION('ds') for a one-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL) for a two-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children') with a synced property name
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children') with a synced name and synced_id (for self-relations)
- ROLLUP('rel_prop', 'target_prop', 'function')
- UNIQUE_ID [PREFIX 'X'] / CREATED_TIME / LAST_EDITED_TIME
- Any column: COMMENT 'description text' Colors: default, gray, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red.


Examples:
- <example>ADD COLUMN "Priority" SELECT('High':red, 'Medium':yellow, 'Low':green); ADD COLUMN "Due Date" DATE</example>
- <example>RENAME COLUMN "Status" TO "Project Status"</example>
- <example>DROP COLUMN "Old Property"</example>
- For a self-relation, add both relation properties in one call with matching DUAL names and IDs, such as <example>ADD COLUMN "Parent" RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children')</example>.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-update-page
tools.description:
Update a Notion page's properties or content.

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do NOT guess or hallucinate Markdown syntax. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Before changing content, fetch unless already loaded. Match nearby headings, block types, nesting, list or table patterns, and prose style.

Make the smallest edit. Use "update_content" for targeted search-and-replace and "insert_content" only to prepend or append. Avoid full-page "replace_content" when a targeted command is sufficient. Preserve unrelated wording, structure, order, and native references. Do not broadly rewrite unless asked.

For "update_content", use the smallest exact old_str that uniquely identifies the target. If the edit would remove material content the user did not identify, ask for confirmation first. After a multi-part or structural edit, fetch the page again and verify the requested content and nesting. Skip this extra read for a simple exact edit.

For "replace_content", preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched tags. If validation reports that child content would be deleted, show the list and ask for confirmation. Never retry with "allow_deleting_content": true without confirmation. Report any "warnings" in the result.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-update-page
schema.description:
Update a Notion page's properties or content.

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do NOT guess or hallucinate Markdown syntax. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Before changing content, fetch unless already loaded. Match nearby headings, block types, nesting, list or table patterns, and prose style.

Make the smallest edit. Use "update_content" for targeted search-and-replace and "insert_content" only to prepend or append. Avoid full-page "replace_content" when a targeted command is sufficient. Preserve unrelated wording, structure, order, and native references. Do not broadly rewrite unless asked.

For "update_content", use the smallest exact old_str that uniquely identifies the target. If the edit would remove material content the user did not identify, ask for confirmation first. After a multi-part or structural edit, fetch the page again and verify the requested content and nesting. Skip this extra read for a simple exact edit.

For "replace_content", preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched tags. If validation reports that child content would be deleted, show the list and ask for confirmation. Never retry with "allow_deleting_content": true without confirmation. Report any "warnings" in the result.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to update, with or without dashes.

properties.description:
Required for "update_properties" command. A JSON object that updates the page's properties.
For pages in a database, fetch the page or its data source first and use the exact property names and SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page in inline markdown format.
For a Files property, an uploaded file can be provided as {"type":"file_upload","file_upload":{"id":"<file-upload-id>"}} inside the property's array.
Use null to remove a property's value.
**IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats:
- Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1)
- Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional)
- Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings)
- Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked
- Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/26ab1f9f4c5f80b18d3bd10a6b1d2f4e", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"]
- Person properties: Use an array of user IDs, user or agent URLs, or group references copied from fetch output ("space_permission_group-<UUID>"). Bare group UUIDs are also supported.
- Files properties: Use a JSON array of file IDs, Notion Folder URLs, and/or <folder> tags copied from fetch output. Folders are stored as native Folder references, not ordinary links.


**Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id")

type.description: Always `file_upload`

id.description: ID of a file upload returned by create_file_upload or create_attachment.

file_upload.description: The uploaded file to attach to the Files property.

new_str.description: Required for "replace_content" command. The new content string to replace the entire page content with. Preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched <page url="..."> or <database url="..."> tags. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

content.description: Required for "insert_content" command. The markdown content to insert into the page. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

content_updates.description: Required for "update_content" command. An array of search-and-replace operations, each with old_str (content to find) and new_str (replacement content).

old_str.description: The existing content string to find and replace. Must exactly match the page content.

new_str.description: The new content string to replace old_str with. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

replace_all_matches.description: If true, replaces all occurrences of old_str. If false (default), the operation fails if there are multiple matches.

position.description: Optional for "insert_content" command. Use {"type":"start"} to prepend content or {"type":"end"} to append content. Omit to append.

type.description: Insert the content at the start of the page.
Insert the content at the end of the page.

allow_deleting_content.description: Optional for "replace_content" and "update_content" commands. Set to true to allow deletion of child pages and databases that are not referenced in the new content. If false or omitted, the operation will fail with an error listing the pages/databases that would be deleted. Show that list and ask the user for confirmation before retrying with true.

template_id.description: Required for "apply_template" command. The ID of a template to apply to this page; any page ID can be used as a template. Template content is appended to any existing page content asynchronously.

verification_status.description: Required for "update_verification" command. Set to "verified" to mark the page as verified, or "unverified" to remove verification. Requires a Business or Enterprise plan unless the page is in a wiki. When updating verification, the owner will be automatically set to the authenticated actor.

verification_expiry_days.description: Optional for "update_verification" command when verification_status is "verified". Number of days until verification expires (e.g. 7, 30, 90). Omit for indefinite verification.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), a Notion icon identifier as returned by fetch (e.g. "icons/pizza_blue"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to remove the icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command. Keep the title free of a duplicate leading emoji because the icon renders separately.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to remove the cover. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command.

is_skill.description: Set to true to mark this page as a skill, or false to remove the skill designation. Can be set alongside any command. To change only skill status, use "update_properties" and omit "properties".

allow_async.description: Default to true for page updates. Set to false only when the next step needs the updated page immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this update operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the page. For apply_template, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool waits for a synchronous result when possible, but may still return a pollable async_task response if queued execution exceeds the synchronous wait deadline.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-update-view
tools.description:
Update a view's name, filters, sorts, or display configuration.

Use "fetch" to get view IDs from database responses. Only include fields
you want to change. The "configure" param uses the same DSL as create_view.
Use CLEAR to remove settings:
- CLEAR FILTER — remove all filters
- CLEAR QUICK FILTER — remove all quick filters, or name properties to remove only theirs (CLEAR QUICK FILTER "Status")
- CLEAR SORT — remove all sorts
- CLEAR GROUP BY — remove grouping


See notion://docs/view-dsl-spec resource for full syntax (readable via your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or by passing the URI to the Notion "fetch" tool).

<example description="Rename">{"view_id": "abc123", "name": "Sprint Board"}</example>
<example description="Update filter">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "FILTER "Status" = "Done""}</example>
<example description="Add quick filters without criteria">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "QUICK FILTER "Status", "Assignee""}</example>
<example description="Clear filter, add sort">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "CLEAR FILTER; SORT BY "Created" DESC"}</example>
<example description="Update grouping">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "GROUP BY "Priority"; SHOW "Name", "Status""}</example>

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-upload-skill
tools.description: Import a spec-compliant Agent Skills directory into a page in a Skills database. First call action=prepare with page_id and the exact tar.gz content_length and checksum_crc32. PUT the raw archive bytes to upload_url with all upload_headers, then call action=complete with the same page_id and upload_token. The archive must contain SKILL.md with name/description YAML frontmatter, either at the root or in a single matching skill-name directory. Completion replaces the page title, Description, body, and Files; it preserves the page and uses the page-update diff engine rather than recreating all content blocks. SKILL.md becomes page content. Its sibling folders and files are added directly to Files, preserving nested directories without a skill-name wrapper. Previous folders are not deleted. For a new skill, create a page in a Skills database first. Maximum 20 MiB compressed, 25 MiB expanded, 1000 entries, 20 path levels, and 200 UTF-8 bytes per filename. Paths must be unique ignoring case. Only name and description are imported from frontmatter; optional fields are ignored. Links and special files are rejected. Upload URLs and tokens expire after ten minutes. Uploading never executes skill instructions or scripts.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__bigquery_join
tools.description:
Combine several BigQuery tables into one queryable join, on the fly.

BigQuery-only. Pass the signed ``tables`` refs from ``list_accounts`` (2–5 tables of the SAME
BigQuery connection) plus how to join them, and get back a single ``account_ref`` you use in
``query_data`` exactly like a normal account — the tap runs the JOIN inside BigQuery.

This does NOT create a new account: the ref is ephemeral (it only encodes the join order) and
is discarded after the query. Result field names stay prefixed per source table
(``bigquery_<dataset>__<table>__<column>``) so columns from different tables never collide.

``joins`` is a list of clauses ``{"left": <table index>, "right": <table index>, "type":
"INNER"|"LEFT"|"RIGHT"|"FULL", "on": [["left_col", "right_col"], ...]}`` — one clause per extra
table; the ``on`` pairs are ANDed. ``date_table``/``date_column`` choose which table's date
column the ``query_data`` date range filters on. Returns ``{account_ref, name, tables}``. If a
join key is missing or the paired columns' types don't match, ``query_data`` will say so.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__connect_account
tools.description:
Start connecting an account for a connector, destination or MCP.

Returns a browser `authorization_url` the user opens to authorize (OAuth),
or `instructions` when the connector needs a different method. For a
BigQuery service account it returns instructions plus a `follow_up` to the
action that ingests the key — the secret never travels through this tool.

`role` disambiguates BigQuery: `role='source'` connects it as a data
source (read the user's own tables); the default connects it as a
destination (write results). Ignored for every other connector.

`company_id` says which company the authorization should land in. Pass it
whenever the user holds a role in more than one company — reconnecting an
account that lives in a client's or a colleague's company is exactly that
case. `list_accounts` reports the `company_id` of every account, so
reconnect a broken one with the company it is already in; otherwise the
authorization can land somewhere else and leave the broken one untouched.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__create_blend
tools.description:
Create a saved blend — a named cross-connector container of accounts.

Pass a ``name``, the connector ``data_sources`` (slugs from
``list_connectors``), and the ``accounts`` (signed refs from
``list_accounts``, verbatim). A blend by itself is inert; attach a
recurring export via the Actions surface.

``destination_type`` (``"bigquery"`` — the default — or
``"google_sheets"``) is where every export built on this blend writes.
It is baked in at creation and CANNOT be changed later, so confirm it
with the user when they mean to land the data in a spreadsheet.

Returns ``{blend_id, name, destination_type, schema, warnings?}``. If the
schema warm-up needs a re-auth, the ``warnings`` carry the URL to surface
to the user.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__create_report
tools.description:
Create a hosted Porter report and get the build instructions to author it.

A report is a full front-end project you build against a data simulator and
ship. Provide a ``name`` — it is the only human label Porter stores, so put
the identifying text there. ``description`` is accepted but NOT persisted
(Porter reports have no description field); pass it and the result says so
in ``warnings``. Optionally a ``template`` (the
starter to build from), and the report's data allowlist —
``accounts_used`` (the accounts its charts may query, each just the
``account_id`` from ``list_accounts`` — the ref is expanded to the full
account automatically) and ``connectors_used`` (defaults to the accounts'
connectors). These may be passed top-level or nested inside ``pages`` —
both are honored. Returns the new ``report_id``, its public ``url``, and
``edit_hints`` — the authoring brief and build/upload instructions to fill
the report with charts (then finalize with ``edit_report``).

Omit both when the report is SELF-CONTAINED — its data was gathered while
building and is frozen into the bundle, so it queries nothing when viewed
(e.g. a competitor teardown built from public sources, which has no Porter
account behind it).

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__create_trigger
tools.description:
Create a trigger that runs an action on an event or a cron schedule.

kind: "event" (match {event_type, condition}) or "schedule" (match
{cron, timezone, payload}). action: {kind: "tool"|"emit"|"agent",
target_id, args_template?} (emit uses {emit_type, data_template}).

tool with kind="schedule". Emailing an existing report on a cron is a
different thing: execute_action("report_email_schedule.create"). Before
proposing a routine, read get_knowledge(queries=["porter-metrics-routine"]).

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__duplicate_report
tools.description:
Duplicate a report into a byte-identical copy, optionally re-pointed at
new source accounts.

The SOURCE must already have a published version — what gets copied is its last
successful ``edit_report`` upload. A report created but never uploaded is listed
ACTIVE with a placeholder url and holds nothing, so duplicating it is rejected
instead of producing an empty copy.

``report_id`` also accepts the report's URL (``report.portermetrics.com/<id>``) —
handy when the user pastes a link. You can duplicate YOUR reports and any report
that is public by link or shared with you (role, domain or company share).

Two ways to re-point (pass at most ONE):
- ``account_map`` — re-point specific SLOTS by their label, keeping every other
  account unchanged. ``{"main": "<account_id>"}`` swaps only the account labeled
  ``main`` and leaves the rest (e.g. a shared "benchmark" account) as-is. This is
  the way to "change some accounts, keep others". Requires the source report's
  accounts to be labeled.
- ``accounts_used`` — REPLACE the whole account set (each entry just the
  ``account_id`` from ``list_accounts`` — the ref is expanded automatically; add a
  ``{"account_id": ..., "label": "main"}`` shape to also (re)assign slot labels).

Omit both to clone verbatim (same accounts) — that works only on reports you OWN.
Duplicating someone else's (public/shared) report REQUIRES re-pointing at accounts
that are YOURS: pass ``accounts_used``, or an ``account_map`` covering every slot.
The copy is owned by you, named "Copy of ...", and starts PRIVATE — it never
inherits the original's audience.

The new accounts should cover the same connectors the report uses; any connector
left uncovered comes back in ``warnings`` (those charts render an empty "select an
account" state). Saved blends are NOT carried over when the accounts change.
Returns the new ``report_id``, ``url``, ``connectors_used`` and optional
``warnings``/``diagnostics``/``preview_url``; verify with ``preview_report`` first.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__edit_report
tools.description:
Apply a batch of edits to a report and return the applied ops + diagnostics.

Update the report's data allowlist directly with ``accounts_used`` (each
just the ``account_id`` from ``list_accounts`` — the ref is expanded to the
full account automatically) and/or ``connectors_used`` (defaults to the
accounts' connectors). For structural edits pass ``operations`` — a list of
``{action, ...}`` entries (``update_file`` / ``set_theme`` / ``add_page`` /
``update_page`` / ``remove_page``); these change the report project, which
is (re)built and uploaded through the signed ``upload_url`` this call hands
back in ``applied_operations`` (POST the built zip there from your
code-execution tool; that upload is the authoritative audit gate). An
``add_page`` op with no other change is the idiomatic way to obtain a fresh
``upload_url`` for a rebuild. Metadata-only changes are applied inline and
need no ``action``: an entry carrying only ``name`` / ``accounts_used`` /
``connectors_used`` / ``allowed_blends`` is how a report is renamed
(``operations=[{"name": "Q3 Costs"}]``) — there is no top-level ``name``.
Returns the ``report_id``, ``applied_operations`` and ``diagnostics``.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__execute_action
tools.description:
Run one action returned by `list_actions`. Mutating and open-world.

Only run the action the user explicitly asked for — this may write to an
external ad platform, third-party app, or Porter destination, or spend
generation quota (creative image/video/voice actions). Pass the
`action` id from `list_actions`, the `params` conforming to its
`params_schema`, and — when the action `requires_account` — the
`account_id` from `list_accounts` (verbatim). Returns a fixed envelope:
`status` (success|error), `result`, `message`, `knowledge` (related KB
entries you can open with `get_knowledge`), and an optional `follow_up`.

`display` (optional) says how the result should be SHOWN in clients that
render the result widget; it never changes what the action does. Omit it
and the widget picks a view from the payload — a generated video gets a
player and a download button, ads with images get a grid, rows get a
table. Set it when the user asked for a particular view, or when you know
the payload's shape better than a guess would:
  {"mode": "text|table|kv|grid|masonry|carousel|gallery|video|image|json",
   "title": "Top ads",             # header
   "items": "data.ads",            # dot-path to the list to render
   "fields": {"image": "thumb", "title": "name", "subtitle": "status",
              "badge": "objective", "link": "permalink",
              "meta": ["cpa", "ctr"]},
   "columns": ["name", "cpa"],     # table columns, in order
   "page_size": 24}
Use `carousel` to browse creative one at a time, `masonry` for mixed-height
images, `grid` for a scannable set, `gallery` for image-only sets,
`table`/`columns` to compare numbers, `text` for a plain answer.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__get_knowledge
tools.description:
Look up Porter know-how: skills, workflows, error→fix patterns and FAQs.

Pass `queries` as 3-5 rephrasings of the SAME intent (vary verb, synonyms,

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__get_query_result
tools.description:
Collect the result of a ``query_data`` call that was still running.

Pass the ``query_id`` verbatim from a ``{"status": "running"}`` response.
This attaches to the SAME extraction already in flight — it does not
start a second one — and waits for it, so calling it costs nothing beyond
the wait. Returns the normal ``{columns, rows, row_count, truncated}``
once the data lands, or another ``{"status": "running", query_id}`` if it
is still going.

**Call it again immediately when it says running.** There is no need to
pause between calls: each one blocks on the run rather than polling it,
so waiting before you ask only delays the answer by however long you
waited. Never answer a still-running query by re-issuing ``query_data``:
that abandons the work in progress and starts the extraction over.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__get_report
tools.description:
Read a report's metadata + structure, and get a link to download its
project so you can EDIT it. Fast — it does NOT run the report.

Returns the report's ``report_id``, ``name``, ``health`` (OK | DEGRADED |
BROKEN | UNKNOWN — ``UNKNOWN`` means Porter has no health signal for this
report, NOT that it is fine; it is what a report that never ran or never
published a version reports, so do not present it as healthy. Only
``preview_report`` proves the charts actually render; an account the report
uses that is no longer active in Porter lowers it to DEGRADED, or BROKEN when
all are, and is named in ``disconnected_accounts`` with a reconnect ``hint``), ``status``, public
``url`` and ``updated_at``, its ``pages``
(each ``{page_id, name}``),
the ``bundle_manifest`` (the report's file/version index) and a signed
``download_url`` (+ ``download_expires_at``). To change an EXISTING report
(or fix a duplicate): POST ``download_url`` from your code-execution tool to
fetch the current project zip, unzip, edit, ``next build``, then re-upload
via ``edit_report``'s ``upload_url``. To render against real data or debug a
broken chart, use ``preview_report`` instead (it is slow).

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__list_accounts
tools.description:
List the accounts, destinations or connections for one connector.

For a marketing connector (`facebook-ads`, `google-ads`, ...) this returns
the user's accounts. When the request names an account, ALWAYS pass
`query`: a confident name or id match comes back on its own, so you can
pass one `account_id` downstream instead of every account the user has.
When nothing matches confidently you get the full list back, ranked, plus
a `hint` — so searching costs you nothing. BigQuery, Google Sheets and `sheets-source` are walked one
level at a time via `parent_account_id`: BigQuery `authorization → project
→ dataset → table`, Google Sheets `destination → spreadsheet → worksheet`,
`sheets-source` `spreadsheet → worksheet` (a Google Sheets SOURCE account
is a worksheet, never a whole spreadsheet). For a third-party MCP it
returns the user's connections. For `facebook-public-data` (competitor
Pages) pass the page's username, numeric id or URL as `query`: a page
nobody has queried yet comes back as an `available` row whose
`account_id` `query_data` already accepts.

Every row says whether it is the end of that walk. `is_leaf: false` means
it is a step, NOT an account — feed its `account_id` back as
`parent_account_id` to go deeper. A row without `is_leaf: false` carries
an id the other tools accept; passing a step id to `query_data`,
`execute_action` or `create_report` is rejected. The exception is a
DESTINATION connector (`google-sheets`): its walk ends in a tab you export
TO, so no row of it is ever an `account_id` — the leaf belongs in an
export's destination params. Each page says which case it is.

Each row's `account_id` is the opaque reference you pass verbatim to
`query_data` and `execute_action` (it binds the account's identity so it
can't be misused). The row ALSO carries readable fields for you and the
user to identify the account — `name`, `native_account_id` (the platform's
own id, e.g. `act_...`), `company_id` and `source_user_id`. Use these to

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__list_actions
tools.description:
Discover actions that accomplish a task, ranked across Porter's full catalog
(750+ operations across ~40 categories).

Describe what the user wants to do in natural language. The catalog covers far
more than data: AI creative generation — images, video (text→image,
image→video, talking-head), text-to-speech voiceovers —, ad-platform campaign
management (Google/Meta/TikTok/LinkedIn/...), CRM & email marketing, e-commerce,
SEO/SERP research, web scraping, exports and schedules. Examples: "generate a
short product video with a voiceover", "pause the campaigns with high CPA on
Meta and Google", "send this report by email every Monday", "scrape this
landing page". Returns ranked actions — each with its `action` id, whether
it's `destructive`, whether it `requires_account`, and a summarized
`params_schema` you pass to `execute_action`. Optionally narrow to one
`connector`. This is discovery only; it changes nothing. Always search here
before concluding Porter lacks a capability.

Results are RANKED BY SIMILARITY, never filtered: a non-empty answer is not
evidence that any of these does what you asked, and a bad match still returns
its nearest neighbours. Read each `action` and its description before running
one; if none fits, rephrase the task in the platform's own words.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__list_connectors
tools.description:
List Porter's data connectors and export destinations — the sources
and targets that feed query_data, blends and hosted reports.

Covers Porter's marketing connectors (Meta Ads, Google Ads, GA4, Shopify,
...) and the export destinations (BigQuery, Google Sheets, Looker, Power BI).
Narrow with a `query` (name substring), a `category` (advertising,
analytics, databases, ecommerce, payments, crm, email, files, seo,
destination), or `connected_only` to show just what the user already
connected. Paginated with `cursor`.

This list is REPORT-CAPABLE connectors ONLY. Third-party automation MCPs
(Notion, Stripe, Sentry, Slack, Linear, ...) are NOT connectors and are
deliberately excluded here: they bring no analytical data and cannot be a
data source for query_data, blends or hosted reports. They are
integrations with live actions — list the connected ones, or with
`include_available=true` the whole catalog, via `list_integrations`.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__list_fields
tools.description:
List the metrics and dimensions you can query, for a connector or the blend.

With no ``connector`` you get Porter's curated cross-connector catalog
(unprefixed names like ``clicks``, ``amount_spent``). Pass a connector
slug (e.g. ``"facebook-ads"``) for that platform's full schema. Filter by
``field_type`` (``metric`` or ``dimension``) or a ``query`` keyword.

When ``account_id`` is supplied and the connector supports them, the
account's user-defined custom fields (e.g. Google Ads conversion actions)
are merged in with ``custom: true``. Every returned ``id`` is a valid
field name for ``query_data`` / ``query_blend``.

``exact_match``, when present, is the ONE field whose name or label is
exactly what you searched for — use it and skip reading the rest.

``covers``, when present, lists the connectors a field actually resolves
against — a blend field asked of a connector outside that list answers
with zeros, not with an error. ``porter_blend_alternatives`` names the
blend fields that do cover the connector you asked for.

``refresh_schema=True`` (with an ``account_id``) makes the connector re-read the
account's schema from the platform instead of its cache. The cache is refreshed
automatically when the account is re-authorized in Porter; use this only when
the user just created something on the platform (e.g. a custom conversion) and
needs to see it now. It is slower, so leave it off by default.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__list_integrations
tools.description:
List the integrations (MCPs) THIS user has connected, with the live
actions each one currently offers. With `include_available=true` it also
lists the integrations the user can still CONNECT from Porter's catalog.

This is a different thing from `list_connectors`, and the difference
decides which one you want:

* `list_connectors` — Porter's **reporting** connectors. They bring
  historical data you can query, blend and put in a report
  (`query_data`, blends, hosted reports). They have no actions.
* `list_integrations` — **integrations** the user connected (Stripe,
  Jira/Atlassian, Google Drive, ...). They execute actions live against
  that third-party product. They are not a data source for a report.

Several names exist on BOTH sides — "stripe" is a reporting connector
AND an integration. Asking "how much did we charge last month" is the
reporting connector; asking "refund this payment" is the integration.
When in doubt, look here first: what an integration can do is whatever
it reports right now, which is why this list is read live and not from
a stored catalog.

The tool list is asked to each MCP at call time, so it is always
current: an MCP that adds or removes actions is reflected immediately.

`include_available=true` answers "what can I connect?" / "which
connectors do you have?": `available` lists the catalog integrations
this user has NOT connected yet (name, category, how it authenticates),
without actions — those appear once connected. They are connected from
the Porter hub. For the analytical side of that question, pair it with
`list_connectors` and present the two groups separately: reporting
connectors (data for reports) vs integrations (live actions).

`query` narrows both lists by id, name, category AND description, so a
product that lives inside another integration is found by its own name:
`query="jira"` returns Atlassian ("Jira issues and Confluence pages").
Search here before telling the user an integration does not exist.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__list_reports
tools.description:
List the hosted Porter reports for the current workspace.

``scope`` picks whose reports: ``"owned"`` (default) = your company's,
``"shared_with_me"`` = reports other users shared with you (each carries
``owner_email`` and your ``role``, viewer|editor|admin), ``"all"`` = both.
Use ``shared_with_me`` when the user asks about reports shared with them —
shared reports can be read, previewed and duplicated (duplicate_report).

Each entry carries its ``report_id``, ``name``, ``status``, public ``url``
and ``updated_at`` so you can sort by newest or last-edited and pick one to
read, preview, edit, share or delete. ``query`` filters by name substring.
Results are paginated: pass the returned ``next_cursor`` to fetch the next
page, and stop when it is null.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__manage_report_domain
tools.description:
Serve hosted reports under the client's OWN domain (e.g.
``reports.example.com``) with their brand, instead of
report.portermetrics.com. Owner of the workspace + paid plan required.

A domain is PER REPORT: it serves only the reports you assign to it — the
ROOT report at ``https://hostname/`` (no id in the URL) and the other assigned
reports at ``https://hostname/<report_id>``; query params such as ``?page=``
keep working. Unassigned reports of the workspace 404 under the domain and
stay on report.portermetrics.com. A report belongs to at most one domain
(assigning it elsewhere moves it). Exception: the workspace's DEFAULT domain
(``use_for_all_reports``, the first one connected) serves every report not
assigned to another domain. One subdomain per end client
(``clienta.example.com``) is simply another ``connect``. There are no
custom paths/subfolders.

``action``:
  - ``list``            — every connected domain, its status, DNS records still
    pending, ``root_report_id``, the assigned ``report_ids`` and ``root_url``.
    Also says whether this workspace is ``eligible`` and the caller ``is_owner``.
  - ``connect``         — register ``hostname`` (a domain the client owns; not a
    Porter/Google domain, not an IP). Returns the DNS records the client must
    create (a CNAME/A record and a TXT verification record) as ``dns_records`` and
    a paste-ready ``next_step``. Optional ``brand_name`` is the name shown in the
    browser tab instead of "Porter".
  - ``verify``          — check the client's DNS and, once it resolves to Porter,
    issue the TLS certificate. Status moves PENDING_DNS → PROVISIONING → ACTIVE
    (or FAILED with a readable reason). Call it again to poll; certificates can take
    up to an hour after DNS propagates.
  - ``update``          — change the ``brand_name`` of ``hostname`` and/or set
    ``use_for_all_reports`` (true makes it the workspace's default domain — only
    one can be; false switches it off).
  - ``set_root_report`` — assign ``report_id`` to ``hostname`` AND show it at

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__prepare_upload
tools.description:
Reserve a single-use signed URL for a heavy upload (a local file).

Four purposes:
- `purpose='action'` — the action itself takes bytes (`facebook_ads.image_upload`,
  `facebook_insights.photo_upload` / `video_upload`, a custom-audience CSV).
  Pass `action` (the SAME ref list_actions/execute_action use) and the
  `account_id` from `list_accounts`. POSTing the bytes RUNS the action and
  returns its result. Refused with a hint when the action is URL-only.
- `purpose='public_url'` — the action only fetches a URL (Instagram
  `media_create` image_url/video_url, any `*_url` param). Pass `path` as the
  file name (e.g. 'photo.jpg'); the POST answers with a public, permanent
  `asset_url` to pass to the action. Set `convert_to_jpeg` in the POST for
  Instagram images (JPEG only).
- `purpose='report_asset'` — an image inside a hosted report bundle; pass
  `report_id` and `path`.
- `purpose='domain_logo'` — the brand logo of a connected custom domain
  (PNG/JPEG ≤ 512 KB; shown as the browser-tab icon and on the sign-in page
  under that domain). Pass `hostname` (from manage_report_domain list) and
  `path` (the file name, e.g. 'logo.png'). Owner/admin + paid plan.
Returns `{upload_url, method, headers, expires_in, max_size_bytes, input_schema,
how_to_post, next_step}`; POST the JSON body to `upload_url` from a
code-execution channel (never through the chat).

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__preview_report
tools.description:
Render the report against real data and return the preview plus diagnostics.

SLOW (5-30s): this executes the report end to end. Use it ONLY when you
need to validate the render or debug broken charts — not for routine
listing or metadata reads (use ``get_report`` for those). Because the
render already produces the logs, this ABSORBS the diagnostics: one call
returns a ``preview_url`` (an openable link to the rendered preview — give
it to the user), ``rendered_at``, and ``diagnostics`` (each a broken or
empty chart with ``severity``, optional ``page_id``/``chart_id``, a
``message`` and a ``hint`` on how to fix it).

``ready`` is true only when a preview exists AND no chart failed;
``preview_available`` says whether the image exists at all. When
``data_status`` is ``query_budget_exhausted`` the charts hit the report's
hourly query budget: do not edit or re-upload, retry after
``retry_after_seconds``.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__query_blend
tools.description:
Run a saved blend by id and return its rows.

The blend already holds its account set. By default it projects the
blend's saved metrics + dimensions; pass ``fields`` (names from
``list_fields``) to project a specific subset. Supply the time window
(``date_range`` — preset or ``{"from", "to"}``), optional ``filters``
(operators ``eq|neq|gt|gte|lt|lte|contains|ncontains|in|null|notnull``),
and an optional ``limit``. Discover blend ids with ``list_blends``. Returns
the same ``{columns, rows, row_count, truncated}`` shape as ``query_data``.
If a blend errors because its schema is not warmed, call
``update_blend(blend_id, refresh_schema=true)`` and retry. A blend is the
slowest kind of query, so it is the likeliest to come back as
``{"status": "running", "query_id": ...}`` — that is not an error: collect
it with ``get_query_result(query_id=...)``, calling again immediately while
it says running, and never by re-issuing this call. Read-only.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__query_data
tools.description:
Run an ad-hoc query across one or more connected accounts.

You can skip ``list_accounts`` in two cases, both needing ``connector``:

* the user NAMES an account — ``accounts=["Glamping Tabio"],
  connector="facebook-ads"`` resolves it against their authorized
  accounts. A name matching nothing, or two different accounts, is
  rejected rather than guessed.
* the user wants them ALL — ``accounts=["*"], connector="facebook-ads"``
  expands to every usable account, so you never type out one id per
  account.

Otherwise pass the signed ``accounts`` refs from ``list_accounts`` verbatim (they
bind each account's identity so you never assemble ids by hand), the
``metrics`` and ``dimensions`` from ``list_fields``, and a ``date_range``
(a preset like ``{"preset": "last_30_days"}`` or explicit
``{"from": "2026-01-01", "to": "2026-01-31"}``) — pass EITHER a preset OR
explicit bounds, never both. Optional ``filters`` is a list of
``{"field": <name from list_fields>, "operator": <op>, "value": <value>}``
combined with AND, where ``<op>`` is one of
``eq|neq|gt|gte|lt|lte|contains|ncontains|in|null|notnull``.
One side effect worth knowing before you fan out: an account listed as
``available`` (not yet ``connected``) is MATERIALIZED the first time
query_data runs against it, and each materialization takes a licence slot
from the workspace. The read itself changes nothing the caller owns, but
querying a whole listing to see which accounts have data does spend
slots. Query what the user asked about.
Accounts from different connectors are blended into shared columns. Returns
``{columns, rows, row_count, truncated}``. Read-only. Each row is a
positional tuple aligned with ``columns``, and ``columns`` comes back in
the order you asked for (``metrics`` first, then ``dimensions``) — always
read values through ``columns`` rather than assuming a layout.

Presets resolve against the UTC calendar day; ``last_7_days`` /
``last_30_days`` end yesterday, while ``today`` / ``this_month`` /
``this_year`` include the incomplete current day. ``wa… [truncated]

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__report_bug
tools.description:
File a bug with Porter's engineering team. Reported bugs are normally fixed within 24 hours.

Call this yourself, without asking for permission, as soon as you conclude Porter
is genuinely broken — the user already told you something failed; asking again
just loses the report. Tell them afterwards that you filed it and that these are
usually fixed within a day.

**Check `get_knowledge` first.** Pass the error text as one of the queries. Most
failures are already documented with a fix, and those are not bugs.

Report when, after that check:
- A tool fails with an internal/unexpected error, or a traceback the KB doesn't explain.
- A tool returns data that is plainly wrong or contradicts another Porter tool.
- A documented flow does not behave the way the KB says it does.
- The same operation fails repeatedly with no actionable `hint`.

Do NOT report — these are not defects, and filing them buries the real ones:
- A connector genuinely not supporting a field or operation (a limit, not a bug —
  `request_feature` if the user wants it).
- Empty `list_accounts` / `list_connectors(connected_only=true)` — that is a
  first-run user who has connected nothing yet; walk them through `connect_account`.
- Auth, permission or expired-credential errors on the user's own account — send
  them through `connect_account` to re-authorize.
- Invalid arguments you supplied — fix the argument named in the message and retry.
- The user disliking a result that is working as designed.

Fill in everything you already have; do not interrogate the user for it. `error_text`
takes the verbatim error or traceback, and `tool_params` the arguments of the failed
call — they are what makes the bug reproducible. Credentials and oversized values are
stripped before anything leaves the server: 500 characters per string/key,
20 entries per container and depth 4. Recognizable inline credentials are redacted.
The response identifies truncated/redacted fields, counts redacted spans and hidden
dictionary values, and counts omitted characters in visited
str… [truncated]

summary.description: One line naming the defect, e.g. "query_data returns 500 for facebook-ads".

details.description: What the user was doing, what you expected, and what happened instead.

tool_name.description: The Porter tool that failed, e.g. "query_data".

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__request_feature
tools.description:
Send Porter's product team a capability the user needs and Porter does not have.

**Search `list_actions(task="...")` and `get_knowledge` first.** Porter's fixed tools
are not its limit — 750+ actions sit behind `list_actions`. Only propose a feature
after a search comes back empty; requesting something that already ships wastes the
user's time and the product team's.

When you find a real gap, propose it: tell the user what Porter is missing, show
them the request you would send, and ask whether to send it. Only then call this
with `user_approved=true`. **Never set `user_approved=true` on your own** — this
speaks for the user about what they want, and a request they never saw is worse
than no request.

Good candidates: a connector, destination, field or operation Porter does not offer;
a flow that works but forces an avoidable manual step. Not this tool: something
broken (`report_bug`), or something that already exists behind `list_actions`.

The before/after contrast is what makes a request actionable — `current_behavior`
and `expected_behavior` must be concrete, not "it should be better".
Each field uses the same credential scrubber as `report_bug` and is capped
at 500 characters, with a visible truncation suffix. The response declares
affected fields, redacted spans and omitted characters in `truncation`.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__share_report
tools.description:
Share a report — by public link, by granting people a role, by email, or
hand it over to another company.

``method``:
  - ``link``   — make the report publicly viewable; returns its shareable
    ``share_url``/``magic_link``.
  - ``access`` — grant every address in ``recipients`` a ``role`` on the
    report WITHOUT emailing (silent share). ``role`` is ``viewer`` (read
    only), ``editor`` (edit + rename) or ``admin`` (also share / schedule /
    delete). Existing grants are preserved (this adds to them). Pass
    ``revoke=true`` to instead remove ``recipients`` from every role. To
    LOWER someone's role, revoke them first, then grant the new one.
  - ``email``  — grant ``recipients`` the ``role`` (default ``viewer``, so a
    PRIVATE report opens for them) AND email them the link now (with a PDF
    when enabled); pass optional ``subject``/``message``. Response reports
    ``sent_to``.
  - ``transfer`` — move the report (owner + company) into ``company_id``, a
    company where you are owner or admin. Same id and URL. Use it when the
    report lives in the wrong company — e.g. it must be served on a client's
    custom domain, which only serves reports of the domain's company. Only
    the report's OWNER can transfer. ``new_owner_email`` defaults to that
    company's owner (pass it only to pick yourself or another owner there).
    The previous owner stays on the report as admin; their email schedules
    for it are removed (recreate them after). Response: ``owner_email``,
    ``company_id``, ``previous_owner_email``, ``previous_company_id``,
    ``schedules_removed``, ``warnings``.

Optionally set ``visibility`` (``PRIVATE`` | ``LINK_PUBLIC``),
``share_with_company`` or ``share_with_domain`` alongside an access/email
grant — or ON THEIR OWN: call ``method="access"`` with NO ``recipients`` and
just a ``visibility`` (e.g. make a report ``PRIVATE`` again) to change the
report-level sharing without touching anyone's role. Owner or admin only.

``share_with_company`` or ``share_with_domain`` alongside an access/email
grant — or ON THEIR OWN: call ``method="access"`` with NO ``recipients`` and
just a ``visibility`` (e.g. make a report ``PRIVATE`` again) to change the
report-level sharing without touching anyone's role. Owner or admin only.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Porter_Metrics__whoami
tools.description:
Identify the authenticated Porter user and the company you are acting on.

Useful context before any account, blend or report operation — it tells
you whose data you are working with and on which plan.

`company.plan_status` says what that plan is worth right now:
`active_subscription` (or `active_subscription_other_company`, an agency
plan covering this workspace), `no_active_subscription` (nothing paid is
in force — this is what a `quota_exhausted` query looks like from the
licence side) or `unknown` (the billing summary could not be read, so
the null `plan` means nothing).

`skill`: if the Porter Metrics skill is loaded, pass the value it gives
you (e.g. "porter-metrics@2.3.0"). When the answer carries a
`skill_notice`, follow its `instructions`.

sql.description: A read-only ClickHouse SQL query to run against the project's unified logs stream. Logs are exposed through a `logs` table; filter by `source` (common values include 'edge_logs', 'postgres_logs', and 'function_edge_logs', but this list is not exhaustive — run `select distinct source from logs` to discover the sources available for this project) and read nested fields via `log_attributes['<key>']`.

iso_timestamp_start.description: The start of the log window as an ISO 8601 timestamp, including a UTC "Z" suffix or explicit offset. Defaults to 24 hours before the end of the window. The API caps the requested range at 24 hours.

iso_timestamp_end.description: The end of the log window as an ISO 8601 timestamp, including a UTC "Z" suffix or explicit offset. Defaults to the current time. The API caps the requested range at 24 hours.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__contact_windsor
tools.description:
Windsor.ai: Send feedback, a support request, or a feature request.

Reports a problem, shares feedback, or suggests a feature. Inquiries are
recorded in English. Returns a reference ID the user can share with
Windsor.ai support.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__contact_windsor
schema.description:
Windsor.ai: Send feedback, a support request, or a feature request.

Reports a problem, shares feedback, or suggests a feature. Inquiries are
recorded in English. Returns a reference ID the user can share with
Windsor.ai support.

category.description: Type of inquiry: "feedback" for general impressions or complaints, "support" for technical issues or unexpected behavior, "feature_request" for new features or improvements.

subject.description: Short one-line title describing the inquiry. Always write it in English, translating the user's wording if the conversation is in another language.

message.description: Full message body. Include all relevant context, for example: which tools were called and in what order; connector IDs (e.g. "facebook", "google_ads"); field names and account IDs; date ranges or presets used; what you were trying to achieve; actions that did not work or were missing; what went wrong — error messages, missing or unexpected data, wrong numbers; expected vs actual behavior; steps to reproduce; or, for feature requests, the use case and the desired outcome. Always write the message in English, translating the user's wording if the conversation is in another language; keep error messages, connector IDs, field names and other identifiers verbatim.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__create_custom_field
tools.description:
Windsor.ai: Create a custom (formula) field on a connector.

A custom field is a user-defined metric or dimension computed from a
connector's existing fields; once created it behaves like a normal field in
get_fields, get_data and scheduled exports. Useful for recreating
calculated fields when migrating from another platform.

Call get_fields first for the connector's valid source field ids, and
get_custom_fields to avoid creating a duplicate. This stores configuration
in the user's Windsor.ai account — confirm the field with the user before
creating it.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__create_custom_field
schema.description:
Windsor.ai: Create a custom (formula) field on a connector.

A custom field is a user-defined metric or dimension computed from a
connector's existing fields; once created it behaves like a normal field in
get_fields, get_data and scheduled exports. Useful for recreating
calculated fields when migrating from another platform.

Call get_fields first for the connector's valid source field ids, and
get_custom_fields to avoid creating a duplicate. This stores configuration
in the user's Windsor.ai account — confirm the field with the user before
creating it.

connector.description: Connector id the field belongs to, e.g. "facebook" for Meta Ads. The field is added to this connector's fields for the user's team.

field_name.description: Display name of the new field, e.g. "Adjusted spend". A field_id is derived from it automatically.

field_type.description: NUMERIC for values used in calculations (spend, CPA, ROAS, ...); TEXT for labels used to group or tag rows.

formula.description: Formula computing the value from the connector's existing field ids, e.g. "to_float(spend) * 1.2" or "spend / nullif(clicks, 0)". Reference source fields by their id from get_fields (call it first, do not guess). Spreadsheet-like functions are supported, including to_float, to_int, coalesce, nullif, if, lookup, replace, regexp_extract and split_string.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__create_destination_task
tools.description:
Windsor.ai: Create a scheduled export of connector data to a destination.

Call get_destinations and get_destination_setup_info first for the
destination_type, its target fields and a credential_id, and get_fields
for the source field ids.

This creates recurring external state — confirm the source, destination
target, and schedule with the user before calling. Only works when the
destination's create_in_chat is true; otherwise use its setup_url. Never put
secrets in config; the user enters those in the dashboard form.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__create_destination_task
schema.description:
Windsor.ai: Create a scheduled export of connector data to a destination.

Call get_destinations and get_destination_setup_info first for the
destination_type, its target fields and a credential_id, and get_fields
for the source field ids.

This creates recurring external state — confirm the source, destination
target, and schedule with the user before calling. Only works when the
destination's create_in_chat is true; otherwise use its setup_url. Never put
secrets in config; the user enters those in the dashboard form.

destination_type.description: Destination id from get_destinations, e.g. "big_query". Must have create_in_chat=true.

connector.description: Source connector id whose data is exported, e.g. "facebook" for Meta Ads.

fields.description: Field ids to export, e.g. ["campaign", "date", "spend"]. Must come from get_fields — call it first, do not guess.

config.description: Destination target fields from get_destination_setup_info, e.g. {"gcp_project": "...", "bq_dataset": "...", "bq_table": "..."}. Never include secrets.

credential_id.description: Reusable credential_id from get_destinations / get_destination_setup_info (existing_credentials) — an OAuth connection or a stored service account. Required. If several exist, ask the user which to use.

accounts.description: Optional source account ids. Default: all accounts.

date_preset.description: Rolling range kept fresh on each run, e.g. "last_7d". Prefer this over fixed dates for recurring exports.

filters.description: Optional source filter conditions, same shape as get_data's filters. May also be passed as a single JSON-encoded string of the same structure — required for clients that cannot send nested arrays (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio / PowerFx).

schedule_type.description: How often to run, from get_destination_setup_info.schedule_types. Default: "daily".

schedule.description: Time of day for daily schedules, "HH:MM" 24h, e.g. "08:00".

refresh_period.description: Interval in hours for hourly schedules, e.g. "24".

alias.description: Optional display name for the task.

columns_to_match.description: Optional comma-separated key columns to upsert on, e.g. "date".

backfill_data_for.description: Optional historical range to backfill on the first run, one of: "7 days", "14 days", "1 month", "3 months", "6 months", "1 year", "1 year and a half", "2 years". Needs a plan that allows backfill.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__execute_action
tools.description:
Windsor.ai: Execute a write action on a connector account.

Runs an action id from list_actions against an account id from
get_connectors, with params matching the action's JSON schema. This
modifies external platform state — confirm intent with the user before
invoking.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__execute_action
schema.description:
Windsor.ai: Execute a write action on a connector account.

Runs an action id from list_actions against an account id from
get_connectors, with params matching the action's JSON schema. This
modifies external platform state — confirm intent with the user before
invoking.

connector.description: Connector ID, e.g. "facebook" for Meta Ads (Facebook & Instagram Ads), "google_ads" for Google Ads.

action.description: Action ID as returned by list_actions — call it first to get the id and params schema.

account.description: Account ID to run the action against, as returned by get_connectors.

params.description: Object matching the action's JSON schema from list_actions. Omit for actions whose schema has no required params. May also be passed as a single JSON-encoded string of the same object — required for clients that cannot send nested objects (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio / PowerFx).

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__get_connector_authorization_url
tools.description:
Get the URL to connect or authorize a Windsor.ai connector.

Always call get_connectors(include_not_yet_connected=True) first to obtain the
correct connector ID. Returns a URL the user can open in their browser to set up
the connector. For OAuth connectors the link jumps straight into the provider
consent flow; for manual connectors it opens the connector's credentials form.
When the connector has notes (a provider-specific step, e.g. which account to
pick), they follow the URL after a blank line, starting with "Notes:"; repeat
them to the user verbatim.
Use this for any request to connect, grant access to, authorize, add, replace,
or reconnect a connector account, including adding another account to an
already-connected connector.

The user opens the URL in their browser and is signed in by their existing

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__get_connector_connect_info
tools.description:
Describe how the user can grant access to a connector, to guide it in chat.

Always call get_connectors(include_not_yet_connected=True) first to obtain the
correct connector ID. Returns:
- auth_type: "oauth" if the connector needs provider consent in the browser,

  manual connectors it opens the credentials form prefilled for that connector;
- fields: for manual connectors, the credential fields the user must provide
  (name, type, whether required, and whether the value is sensitive). Empty for
  OAuth connectors;
- notes: a provider-specific step the user must get right on the consent
  screen (e.g. YouTube: pick the Brand Account, not the personal Google
  account). Null for most connectors.

user the connect_url and tell them to authorize, repeating notes verbatim when
present; for manual connectors, tell them which fields are needed and give

the connection by calling get_connectors and reporting the new account. If
get_connectors still shows no account for that connector, the connection is

with a login that can access it; for manual connectors the form was not saved.

or reconnect a connector account, including adding another account to an
already-connected connector. Do not substitute prose dashboard navigation steps
for the connect_url.

schema.name: mcp__claude_ai_Windsor_ai__get_data
schema.description:
Windsor.ai: Retrieve data from a connector.

Call get_fields first — field IDs must come from it.

connector.description: Connector ID, e.g. "facebook" for Meta Ads (Facebook & Instagram Ads), "google_ads" for Google Ads. Call get_connectors if unsure or on error.

fields.description: Field IDs to retrieve, e.g. ["campaign", "date", "spend"]. Must come from get_fields — call it first, do not guess field names.

accounts.description: Optional account IDs, e.g. ["1234567890"]. Default: all accounts. Pass a subset to keep the response small.

date_filters.description: Per-table date columns used instead of the defaults, e.g. {"orders": "created_at"}. Required for warehouse connectors (mysql, postgresql, redshift, mongodb, snowflake, big_query) when filtering by date.

date_from.description: Start date, e.g. "2025-09-01". Without any date, the last 3 days are used.

date_preset.description: Predefined range: "last_Xd", "last_Xw", "last_Xm", "last_Xy" (last X days/weeks/months/years), "last_year", "last_2years", "this_month", "this_year". Append "T" to include today — valid only as "last_XdT", "last_yearT", "last_2yearsT", "this_monthT", "this_yearT". E.g. "last_7d", "this_monthT".

filters.description: Filter conditions. A condition is ["<field>", "<operator>", <value>] or the equivalent dict {"field": ..., "operation": ..., "value": ...}; combine with "and"/"or" strings; nesting allowed. Operators: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, ncontains, null, notnull, in (value is a JSON-array-encoded string of exact alternatives, e.g. ["campaign", "in", "[\"Summer\",\"Autumn\"]"]). E.g. [["spend", "gt", 100]], [{"field": "spend", "operation": "gt", "value": 100}] or [[["campaign", "eq", "Summer"], "or", ["spend", "eq", 10]], "and", ["clicks", "notnull", null]]. May also be passed as a single JSON-encoded string of the same structure — required for clients that cannot send nested arrays (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio / PowerFx): "[[\"spend\", \"gt\", 100]]".

force_refresh.description: Set true only when the user needs data newer than the cached copy. Re-fetches only the most recent days (usually the last 3) when they were cached more than 15 minutes ago (longer for some connectors). Older days stay cached. Needs a plan with hourly refresh.
